purpose: Control the collection, use, storage, separation and disclosure of personal information within property investigations so only information necessary for the stated investigation purpose is handled.
source_basis: GDPR Article 5 principles as explained by the Irish Data Protection Commission
DPC guidance on data minimisation, purpose limitation, accuracy, storage limitation, integrity/confidentiality and accountability
core_principle: COLLECT THE MINIMUM NECESSARY → USE ONLY FOR THE INVESTIGATION PURPOSE → SEPARATE CITIZEN MATERIAL FROM OFFICIAL RECORDS → RETAIN ONLY AS JUSTIFIED → PROTECT ACCESS
data_minimisation_rules: Request only information necessary to determine the investigation route or answer the stated question.
Do not request identity information merely because it might be useful later.
Do not retain unrelated personal information contained in a document when it is not material to the investigation.
Where a less intrusive identifier can achieve the same investigation purpose, prefer it.
Separate property identifiers from unnecessary personal profiles.
Do not infer or enrich personal information beyond what the investigation requires.
source_separation_rules: Citizen-supplied documents are never relabelled as official records.
Official records retain their originating authority and retrieval provenance.
A citizen document may corroborate an issue but does not automatically establish the official registered position.
Copies, screenshots and photographs remain distinct source objects even when they appear to reproduce an official record.
Derived facts must retain links to the source from which they were derived.
access_rules: Investigation access should be limited to the information needed for the assigned investigation function.
Public answer views should expose only information necessary to explain the answer.
Internal provenance may be retained separately from public presentation where required.
Do not expose unrelated personal information merely because it exists in the case file.
Access restrictions must not be treated as evidence that a record does not exist.
retention_rules: Retention must be tied to the documented purpose and applicable legal obligations.
Do not invent a universal retention period.
Where the purpose ends and no continuing lawful retention requirement applies, the information should enter the appropriate disposal/review process.
Retention and deletion decisions must be auditable.
Legal claims, statutory duties or other applicable requirements may affect retention and must be assessed separately.
accuracy_rules: Record the source and provenance of citizen-supplied personal information.
Do not silently convert allegations or assertions into established facts.
Where personal data are material and inaccurate, route the issue through the applicable correction/review process.
Preserve the distinction between what a person states and what an official record establishes.
hard_stops: Never collect personal information simply because it may become useful.
Never publish personal information merely because it appears in a source.
Never treat citizen-supplied personal information as official property evidence.
Never infer sensitive characteristics from property-investigation data.
Never invent retention periods or legal bases.
Never conceal the presence of material personal-data handling behind a generic evidence label.
